Executive Summary
Woodward Iodine Corporation
Risk Management Plan (40 CFR Part 68)
________________________________________
1. Accidental Release Prevention and Emergency Response Policies
Woodward Iodine Corporation is committed to protecting employees, the community, and the environment from accidental releases of hazardous chemicals. The facility maintains a comprehensive Accidental Release Prevention Program and Emergency Response Program in accordance with EPAs Risk Management Program (40 CFR 68) and OSHAs Process Safety Management (29 CFR 1910.119) requirements.
The facility has established safety policies, operating procedures, training programs, emergency shutdown systems, and mechanical integrity practices to minimize the likelihood and consequences of accidental releases. Emergency response policies are documented in the facilitys Standard Operating Procedures and Emergency Response Plan and are reviewed annually with employees.
________________________________________
2. Regulated Substances Handled
The facility stores and uses the following EPA-regulated substances in quantities above their respective thresholds:
Chemical	CAS No.	Maximum Inventory (lbs.)	Threshold Quantity (lbs.)
Chlorine	7782-50-5	79,000	2,500
Sulfur Dioxide	7446-09-5	78,000	5,000
Anhydrous Ammonia	7664-41-7	72,000	10,000
These substances are stored in dedicated storage tanks located within the secured facility perimeter. Each tank is monitored with surveillance cameras, protected by engineered barriers, and equipped with remote emergency shutdown capabilities accessible both near the tank and in the plant control room.



________________________________________
3. Offsite Consequence Analysis (OCA)
(Summary Only  Details Contained in RMP Submittal)
Woodward Iodine Corporation conducted a Worst-Case Release Scenario and an Alternative Release Scenario for each regulated substance, in accord with EPA requirements.
	Worst-Case Release Scenario: Assumes a catastrophic vessel failure

resulting in complete release of the maximum quantity. This scenario, although highly unlikely, is provided to satisfy regulatory requirements.
	Alternative Release Scenario: Based on the facilitys 2025 Process Hazard Analysis, the most credible event is activation of a pressure relief valve during an overfill of a storage tank, resulting in an estimated 10-minute release until pressure decreases and the relief valve reseats.
Both scenarios were modeled with EPA-approved methods and are detailed in the RMP submission.
________________________________________
4. General Accidental Release Prevention Program
Woodward Iodine Corporation has implemented a full Program 3 prevention program, which includes:
4.1 Process Safety Information (PSI)
	Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) for Cl?, SO?, and NH?
	Detailed process descriptions, equipment specifications, and design codes
	Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs) and process flow diagrams
	Maximum intended inventories and safe operating limits
	Documentation of physical and chemical hazards
4.2 Process Hazard Analysis (PHA)
	PHAs conducted for chlorine, sulfur dioxide, and anhydrous ammonia systems
	Evaluation of potential causes and consequences of accidental releases
	Recommendations tracked to completion
	Updated at least every five years


4.3 Operating Procedures
	Written SOPs for startup, operation, shutdown, emergency isolation, post-shutdown recovery, and temporary operations. 
	Procedures reviewed and certified annually
	Continuous improvement based on operational experience
4.4 Training Program
	Initial and refresher training for operators and maintenance personnel who have been trained in operations. 
	Documentation of competency and evaluation of understanding
4.5 Mechanical Integrity Program
	Inspection, testing, and preventive maintenance of storage tanks, piping, valves, instrumentation, and emergency shutdown systems
	Equipment deficiency tracking and corrective action protocols
4.6 Manageme

nt of Change (MOC)
	Formal review of process or equipment modifications
	Evaluation of safety impacts and updated procedures
4.7 Incident Investigation
	Investigations conducted for all incidents and near-miss events
	Root cause identification and documented corrective actions
4.8 Compliance Audits
	Triennial audits performed to assess compliance with RMP/PSM standards
	Findings documented and resolved through corrective action program
	PHA Audit performed at least every 5 years. 
________________________________________
5. Five-Year Accident History
Woodward Iodine Corporation has had no accidental releases in the past five years that resulted in injuries, evacuations, offsite impacts, or emergency response from local agencies.
________________________________________
6. Emergency Response Program
The facility maintains a written Emergency Response Plan consistent with:
	EPA Risk Management Program (40 CFR 68)
	OSHA Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER) (29 CFR 1910.120)
	Coordination with local emergency responders
Key features include:
	Procedures for notification, evacuation, and emergency isolation
	Site maps showing hazardous chemical locations, evacuation routes, and assembly areas
	Coordination and annual notification exercises with the Woodward Fire Department
	Regular emergency drills and training for employees
	Readily accessible emergency equipment and remote shutdown systems
________________________________________
7. Planned Changes to Improve Safety
Woodward Iodine Corporation is committed to continual safety improvement. Planned enhancements include:
	Implementing recommendations from the most recent PHA
	Completing corrective actions identified during the latest RMP compliance audit
	Updating procedures, training materials, and maintenance programs to reflect best practices
	Enhancing emergency response coordination with local agencies
	Implementing additional detection, interlocks, or alarm upgrades as par

t of continuous improvement
________________________________________
8. Summary
Woodward Iodine Corporation maintains a robust accidental release prevention and emergency response program. Through adherence to EPA and OSHA regulations, engineering safeguards, strict procedures, and ongoing training, the facility strives to ensure the safety of employees, emergency responders, and the surrounding community
